nodes.name: Molten-salt in situ boronization (850°C)
nodes.procedure: B powder was used as B source to conduct the boronation of commercial WS2 under the high-temperature (850 °C) molten-salt condition (KCl:NaCl = ~1:2 molar ratio), realizing the in situ transformation for a part of WS2 to WB2 and thus forming a WB2@WS2 heterostructured catalyst.

unit_operations.name: Boronization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: B powder was used as B source to conduct the boronation of commercial WS2 under the high-temperature (850 °C) molten-salt condition (KCl:NaCl = ~1:2 molar ratio)

nodes.source_text: Figure 1a shows the schematic diagram of synthesizing the boride@sulfide heterostructured catalyst. In this synthesis process, B powder was used as B source to conduct the boronation of commercial WS2 under the high-temperature (850 °C) molten-salt condition (KCl:NaCl = ~1:2 molar ratio), realizing the in situ transformation for a part of WS2 to WB2 and thus forming a WB2@WS2 heterostructured catalyst with compact interfaces between as-formed WB2 and unreacted WS2.

nodes.name: Molten-salt boronization (1000°C)
nodes.procedure: Pure-phase WB2 catalyst was synthesized by raising the temperature to 1000 °C on the basis of the molten-salt method using B powder and commercial WS2.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, the pure-phase WB2 catalyst was synthesized by raising the temperature to 1000 °C on the basis of the above molten-salt method.

properties.description: Shows the electrocatalytic performance (current density vs. potential) of WB₂@WS₂ under varying alkaline pH conditions.
properties.performance_metric_reference: 0.5 mA/cm² (This label likely indicates a target current density for overpotential comparison, though not explicitly marked on the y-axis with a horizontal line in the provided graph).

properties.description: The potential required to achieve a given current density (e.g., -10 mA/cm²) shifts to less negative (more positive) values as the pH increases from 12.5 to 14. This indicates improved electrocatalytic activity (lower overpotential) for WB₂@WS₂ in more alkaline environments.
properties.observed_effect: Improved electrocatalytic activity with increasing pH.

nodes.source_text: The activity of WB2@WS2 exhibits no significant change at 10 mAcm-2... ICP-OES result exhibits that the leached W metal content for WB2@WS2 catalyst is less than 3% during the stability test for 100 h.

visual_evidence.name: Short-term Stability Test of Multiple Catalysts

properties.relative_performance: WS₂ shows the lowest potential (best performance), followed by WB₂-WS₂, then WB₂.

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency measurement for hydrogen generation
nodes.source_text: WB2@WS2 exhibits a high Faradaic efficiency FE) approaching 100% at the current density of 20 mA cm-2.

nodes.description: Desorption experiment of underpotential deposited hydrogen to probe binding energy
nodes.source_text: the hydrogen binding potential of WB2@WS2 is 0.151 V versus RHE, which is lower than those of WS2 (0.415 V), WB2 (0.261 V), and WB2-WS2 (0.314 V).

nodes.description: Screening of 9 transition metal boride@sulfide heterostructured catalysts for HER activity
nodes.source_text: WB2@WS2 possesses a much lower overpotential than those of TiB2@Ti3S4, ZrB2@ZrS3, HfB2@HfS3, VB2@V3S4, NbB2@NbS2, TaB2@TaS2, CrB2@Cr2S3, and MoB2@MoS2 at 10 mA cm-2
WB2@WS2 also displays excellent catalytic performance in acidic (0.5 M H2SO4 solution)
WB2@WS2 also displays excellent catalytic performance in... neutral conditions (1.0 M K2HPO4 + 1.0 M KH2PO4 solution)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm hexagonal structures for WS2 (JCPDS 04-004-0730) and WB2 (JCPDS 04-003-6624). The heterostructure shows peaks for both phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns in Figure 1b indicate the formation of WS2 ... and WB2 ... The WB2@WS2 contains two series of XRD diffraction peaks of WB2 and WS2

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images reveal that the morphologies of the nine boride@sulfide heterostructured catalysts are nanoparticles with a size of 100-500 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that the morphologies of the above nine boride@sulfide heterostructured catalysts are nanoparticles with a size of 100 - 500 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images of WB2@WS2 show compact interfaces with lattice spacings of 0.260 nm (WB2 100), 0.153 nm (WB2 110), 0.228 nm (WS2 103), and 0.185 nm (WS2 105).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image displays the existence of compact interfaces between WS2 and WB2 ... lattice spacing of 0.260 and 0.153 nm ... lattice spacing of 0.228 and 0.185 nm

properties.description: Image showing crystalline phases and their interfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS analysis shows work functions of 7.38 eV, 6.33 eV, and 6.66 eV for WS2, WB2, and WB2@WS2, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) exhibits that work functions of WS2, WB2, and WB2@WS2 are 7.38, 6.33, and 6.66 eV, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms W, B, and S elements; the W 4f7/2 binding energy for WB2@WS2 (31.88 eV) is intermediate between WB2 (31.61 eV) and WS2 (32.64 eV), signifying electron transfer from WS2 to WB2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The binding energy of W 4f7/2 for WB2@WS2 is higher than that of WB2 while it is lower than that of WS2, further demonstrating the occurrence of electron transfer from WS2 to WB2 in WB2@WS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: W L3-edge XANES spectra for WB2@WS2 shows an absorption edge between W foil and WO3, indicating an electron-deficient local environment for W atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the adsorption edge energy of X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy for W L3-edge of WB2@WS2 catalyst is higher than that of W foil and lower than that of WO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS of WB2@WS2 shows three peaks at 2.28, 2.38, and 3.00 Å, corresponding to W-B, W-S, and W-B/S-W bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectroscopy ... exhibit three peaks at approximately 2.28, 2.38, and 3.00 Å which are attributed to W-B, W-S, and W-B/S-W bonds, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: WB2@WS2 exhibits a higher Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area compared to WS2, WB2, and the physical mixture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of WB2@WS2 are larger than those of WS2, WB2, and WB2-WS2

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) of WB2@WS2 is higher than its constituent phases and the physical mixture, indicating more active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of WB2@WS2 are larger than those of WS2, WB2, and WB2-WS2, suggesting the exposure of more active sites

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS spectra show WB2@WS2 has the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct), indicating the fastest reaction kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS spectra in Figure S45 reveal that WB2@WS2 has the smallest charge transfer resistance compared to WB2-WS2, WB2, and WS2

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES analysis shows less than 3% leached W metal after 100 hours of stability testing for WB2@WS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) result exhibits that the leached W metal content for WB2@WS2 catalyst is less than 3% during the stability test for 100 h

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows WS2 vibrational modes at 353 and 421 cm-1 and an OH* intermediate peak at 702 cm-1; WB2@WS2 shows optimal OH* adsorption/desorption dynamics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectra during HER ... shows three well-resolved peaks located at 353, 421, and 702 cm-1, which were attributed to E12g(Γ) bond of WS2, A1g(Γ) bond of WS2, and hydroxyl intermediate for WS2@WB2 catalyst

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show that the nine boride@sulfide catalysts are nanoparticles with sizes ranging from 100 to 500 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that the morphologies of the above nine boride@sulfide heterostructured catalysts are nanoparticles with a size of 100 - 500 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS analysis allows visualization of the W-S and W-B atom configurations in WB2@WS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The wavelet transform EXAFS (WT-EXAFS) analysis further demonstrates the visualization of the W-S and W-B atom configuration in WB2@WS2 catalyst (Figure S26d,e).

nodes.characterization_summary: The Zeta potential of WB2@WS2 (22.7 mV) is higher than that of the WB2-WS2 mixture (11.5 mV), indicating a stronger built-in electric field.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Zeta potential of WB2@WS2 catalyst (22.7 mV) is significantly higher than that of WB2-WS2 catalyst (11.5 mV).

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV curves show overpotentials at 10 mA cm-2 decreasing in the order: WS2 > WB2-WS2 > WB2 > WB2@WS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) curves ... exhibit the overpotentials at 10 mA cm-2, which display a decreased trend in the order of WS2, WB2-WS2, WB2, and WB2@WS2.

nodes.evidence_snippet: WB2@WS2 exhibits a much lower Tafel slope than WB2, WB2-WS2, and WS2 (Figures 2d and S44), suggesting the fast reaction kinetics toward HER.
